title: How to Submit an MCP Server to Muse
summary: Submit an MCP server to Muse with a screenshot walkthrough of Overview, Technical specs, and Review, including the fields and assets to prepare.
body_markdown:
Muse accepts connector submissions through the[Muse Connector Platform](https://muse.ai/platform) . If you already run an MCP server, you can submit its hosted endpoint for review. Approved connectors appear in Muse's directory.


## Before you start


Have these ready:


- Your hosted MCP endpoint and API or MCP documentation.
- A connector name, product website, and example prompts.
- A **512 × 512 PNG or SVG** connector icon.
- Your work email, support contact, privacy policy, and terms of service.
- Details about authentication and any restrictions on access.


Test the endpoint and the prompts you plan to include.[Manufact Publishing Checks](https://manufact.com/platform/publishing-checks) can help identify MCP issues before submission.


Open[muse.ai/platform](https://muse.ai/platform) and click **Submit a connector** . If you are signed out, the platform asks you to sign in or create an account with your work email. The form has three steps: **Overview** , **Technical specs** , and **Review** .


## Step 1: Overview


Enter the **Connector name** , **Company or developer** , and **Product website** . Under **Example prompts** , write requests your connector can handle, such as “Find wooden puzzles for children aged 6 and up” or “Show building sets under $30.”


Upload your icon, then choose whether the connector accepts payments.


The rest of Overview asks for **Your name** , **Work email** , **Support email or URL** , **Your privacy policy** , and **Your terms of service** . The email field explicitly asks for a company email address. Use **Anything else?** for optional context, then click **Next** .


## Step 2: Technical specs


Under **Connection type** , select **Existing MCP** . The form defaults to **Raw API** , which has an API URL and an optional OpenAPI specification field. For an MCP server, enter your deployed URL in **Hosted MCP endpoint** .


Add the **API or MCP documentation** URL. In **Access requirements** , explain anything that affects who can use the connector or what it can do, such as a required account, paid plan, regional availability, or rate limits.


**Authentication methods** is optional and offers **API keys** , **OAuth with PKCE** , and **Other** . Select the methods your server supports, or leave them unchecked if authentication is not required.


Click **Next** to inspect the completed form.


## Step 3: Review


Check the listing details and technical information. Each section has an **Edit** button for corrections.


The final checkboxes ask you to confirm that you are authorized to submit the connector and its brand assets, acknowledge that submission does not guarantee approval, and agree to the **Muse Connector Terms** linked in the form. Promotion depends on usage and editorial discretion.


Read the terms and complete the acknowledgments, then click **Submit for review** to join the review queue.


## What happens after submission?


Muse reviews connectors for functional, security, and legal requirements and performs end-to-end testing. Once approved, a connector can appear in the directory. Featured placement is a separate editorial decision.


For other directories, see our guides to[submitting an MCP app to ChatGPT](https://manufact.com/blog/publish-mcp-app-on-chatgpt) and[submitting an MCP server to Anthropic's directory](https://manufact.com/blog/submit-mcp-server-to-anthropic-directory) .
